title: Driverless Taxi Service Planned for Tokyo in 2027
paragraphs: If you take a taxi in Tokyo next year, you may find that there is nobody in the driver's seat.
US company Waymo plans to launch Japan's first driverless taxi service in Tokyo in 2027. It's working with Tokyo's biggest taxi company, Nihon Kotsu, and taxi-hailing app company GO.
The service will start small, with plans to grow to 100 cars. Passengers will be able to book a ride through either the GO or Waymo app.

Each company will bring something different to the project. Waymo will provide the robotaxi technology, while Nihon Kotsu will handle the day-to-day operations and help customers. GO, which runs Japan's most widely used taxi-hailing app, will help introduce the service to the country's taxi industry.
The partnership began in 2024. Since 2025, the companies have been testing the technology on public roads in seven Tokyo wards. The vehicles use AI, cameras and radar to help them navigate.

At a news conference, the companies said safety was their top priority. They also hope the service can help fill a gap: Japan needs more drivers as its shrinking population leaves businesses struggling to find workers.

But the companies still have an important step ahead: getting government approval. Japan has previously allowed driverless buses to carry passengers along fixed routes. Approving a driverless taxi service, however, would be a first for the country.

And Waymo isn't the only company with its eyes on Tokyo's streets. Japanese carmaker Nissan is working with Britain's Wayve and Uber Technologies on another robotaxi project. They plan to begin test drives in Tokyo later this year.
